title: Unconventional quantum spin mixing of two spin-1 atoms beyond the single-mode approximation
authors: Yanhong Liu, Fulin Deng, Haoxue Qiao, Wenxian Zhang
abstract: The single-mode approximation (SMA) has been widely employed in ultracold spinor gases, where all spin components share the same spatial mode. By adopting generalized Van Vleck (GVV) perturbation theory, we achieve a relative error of $10^{-6}$ in the ground-state energy with a reduced effective Hilbert space dimension of $\sim 10^3$ for two spin-1 bosons confined in a one-dimensional hard-wall trap. With the accurate GVV method, we explore the validity of the SMA across ground-state properties and quench spin dynamics for two $^{7}\text{Li}$, $^{87}\text{Rb}$, or $^{23}\text{Na}$ atoms. Numerical results show that the quadratic Zeeman energy $q$ provides a powerful control knob: by increasing $|q|$, the fidelity between the spin components in the ground state gradually decreases, leading eventually to the breakdown of the SMA (due to the competition between the kinetic energy and the quadratic Zeeman energy). Quench spin dynamics with abruptly increased $q$ further reveals multiple resonances, where the SMA-predicted micromotion and beyond-SMA macromotion appear simultaneously. These results point to a direction to investigate the quantum spin-mixing dynamics beyond the SMA, particularly in recent experiments of strongly interacting spin-1 atomic gases.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes quantum spin mixing in two spin-1 atoms beyond the Single-Mode Approximation using advanced perturbation theory. The authors demonstrate that the quadratic Zeeman energy ($q$) controls the validity of simplified models, showing that large $|q|$ causes the SMA to fail. This failure is evidenced by discrepancies in both the ground-state spatial structure and the complex, multi-timescale dynamics observed during quantum quenches.
main_problem: The study investigates unconventional quantum spin mixing in two spin-1 atoms, specifically analyzing the breakdown of the Single-Mode Approximation (SMA) when considering higher-order spatial correlations.
main_result: The SMA fails when the quadratic Zeeman energy ($q$) becomes large, as this energy competes with the kinetic energy, leading to observable differences in ground-state fidelity and dynamic resonances compared to SMA predictions.
method: The authors employ Generalized Van Vleck (GVV) perturbation theory to accurately solve the many-body Hamiltonian, comparing these results against the simpler SMA and traditional Exact Diagonalization (ED).
model_or_system: The system consists of two spin-1 bosonic atoms (e.g., $^{7}	ext{Li}, ^{87}	ext{Rb}, 	ext{ or } ^{23}	ext{Na}$) confined in a 1D hard-wall trap. The Hamiltonian includes spin-dependent interactions and Zeeman shifts ($p$ and $q$).
key_observables: Quantum fidelity ($F$), normalized single-particle spatial density distribution ($n_{m_F}(x)$), and time evolution of population fractions ($p_{m_F}(t)$).
important_parameters: The quadratic Zeeman energy ($q$) acts as the primary control knob, determining the validity regime of the SMA.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is the use of GVV perturbation theory, which is highly accurate but has a finite range of validity controlled by the perturbative parameter $\eta_g$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the convergence of the GVV method versus ED, show the decay of quantum fidelity $F$ as $|q|$ increases, and compare the predicted time evolution of population fractions, revealing distinct micromotion and macromotion regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the Hamiltonian and the GVV method for accurate ground-state calculations. It then systematically analyzes the ground-state properties by tracking the quantum fidelity $F$ as a function of $q$. Finally, it examines quench spin dynamics, comparing the full GVV results against the SMA predictions to pinpoint resonance structures.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical benchmark for interpreting experimental measurements in strongly interacting spinor Bose-Einstein condensates, showing precisely where mean-field or simplified approximations break down.
